points: It displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was very angry.

note.label: Jonah 4: The Gourd and the Question at the End

points: He said, Was not this my saying when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

note.label: Jonah 4: The Gourd and the Question at the End

points: Take, I beseech thee, my life from me; for it is better for me to die than to live. Then said the Lord, Doest thou well to be angry?

note.label: Jonah 4: The Gourd and the Question at the End

points: Jonah went out of the city, and sat on the east side of the city, and made him a booth, and sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would become of the city.

note.label: Jonah 4: The Gourd and the Question at the End

points: The Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, to be a shadow over his head, to deliver him from his grief; so Jonah was exceeding glad of the gourd.
God prepared a worm when the morning rose the next day, and it smote the gourd that it withered; and he prepared a vehement east wind, and the sun beat upon the head of Jonah, that he fainted.
Thou hast had pity on the gourd, for the which thou hast not laboured, neither madest it grow, which came up in a night, and perished in a night.
And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
